title: What If the Measles Vaccine Stopped Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if the measles vaccine stopped tomorrow? The numbers before it existed are brutal.
In the year 2000, measles killed an estimated 800,000 people worldwide.
By 2023, vaccination had cut that to about 107,000 deaths a year. A drop of more than eighty-five percent.
Over those 23 years, vaccination is estimated to have prevented about 60 million deaths.
Measles is among the most contagious diseases known. When vaccination slips, it's usually the first to come back.
So stopping the shots wouldn't pause anything. It would bring back a disease we already know how to beat.
